dissents.topic: Severity of the missing invariant/specification for the HAS_TIME fast-path predicate

positions.position: P1 — the optimization is TESTED-NOT-PROVED; the author has not written down the invariant that HAS_TIME.test(v) === false implies valueParser would find no time values, and correctness rests on the test suite rather than proof. Acceptance is conditional on adding the precondition comment and/or tightening the regex.
P1 — UNDER-AUDITED; the invariant is sound but unstated, and a one-line literate comment is needed to convert the optimization from opaque to verifiable by inspection.
P2 — ADT-SOUND; the precondition is load-bearing but undocumented, a spec-hygiene note rather than a correctness blocker. Safe to merge.
P2 (implicit) — no correctness risk because the regex is a superset of real time values; concerns are about naming and that the larger complecting is untouched. Ship.
P2 — ACCEPT; loose pre-filter is the right call for a guard, just deserves a one-line comment. Not a blocker.
P2 — SMALL-AND-COMPOSABLE; naming is slightly misleading but does not block merge.

dissents.topic: Whether a benchmark/measurement should be required for this performance fix

positions.position: Yes — no measurement is reported; a before/after number on a representative corpus would elevate this from 'plausible' to 'demonstrated.' Standard Knuth complaint about performance fixes.
Does not require benchmark numbers — the diff is 'small, obvious, and the next maintainer won't curse anyone.' ACCEPT as-is.
Does not require benchmark — accepts the change as a legitimate local guard at the edge of the hot loop given the obvious cost model.
Does not require benchmark — calls it 'measurement-driven optimization applied to the obvious bottleneck' without demanding numbers in the PR.

dissents.topic: Whether to also push the property-name filter earlier

positions.position: Notes the next move is still available — the rule body still complects scope-check with parse-and-walk; a property-name filter before parse would compose with this change.
Treats the existing reorder of propertyName after the fast-path as sound code motion worth confirming explicitly; does not call for further restructuring.
Calls the current ordering correct (unprefix moved past the early-return); suggests promoting to a shared helper on the second copy rather than further restructuring this rule.

issues.description: Fast-path predicate HAS_TIME is under-specified — invariant relating regex to valueParser semantics is not stated or proved
issues.detail: The regex /\dm?s/i is introduced as a cheap pre-filter before the expensive valueParser call, but the author has not written down the load-bearing invariant: HAS_TIME.test(v) === false implies valueParser(v) would yield no time values for this rule. The implication is sound for canonical CSS time syntax (every <time> token is <number><unit> where unit is s or ms, so it must contain a digit adjacent to s or ms), but the proof is left for the reader to reconstruct. Without a one-line comment naming the precondition, correctness rests on the test suite rather than on reasoning — TESTED-NOT-PROVED. A future maintainer extending time syntax (calc(), unit-less zero handling) could silently weaken the postcondition.

issues.description: Constant name HAS_TIME overstates what the regex actually decides
issues.detail: The name reads as a definite predicate ('this value contains a time'), but /\dm?s/i is a conservative over-approximation — it admits false positives like 'foo1s', '1sigma', or digit-then-s inside url(), strings, custom properties, var() fallbacks, or identifiers. That asymmetry (no false negatives, harmless false positives) is the entire point of a fast-path, but the identifier promises more than it delivers. Renaming to MAY_CONTAIN_TIME, LIKELY_HAS_TIME, MAYBE_HAS_TIME, or PREFILTER_TIME — or a one-line comment ('cheap prefilter; real parsing happens below') — would align the name with the postcondition and prevent a future caller from treating it as authoritative.

issues.description: No measurement reported to justify the performance claim
issues.detail: The changeset reads 'Fixed: time-min-milliseconds performance' but includes no before/after numbers, profiler output, or benchmark on a representative corpus. The optimization is almost certainly in the critical 3% (valueParser is expensive; most declarations have no time component), but Knuth's discipline is measure-before-optimize and report the measurement. A one-line note ('on corpus X, rule time dropped from N ms to M ms') would lift this from 'plausible' to 'demonstrated.'

issues.description: Reordering of propertyName computation after the fast-path is sound but worth confirming explicitly
issues.detail: vendor.unprefixed(decl.prop.toLowerCase()) was previously called unconditionally; it is now called only when HAS_TIME matches. Both calls are pure with no side effects, so this is a correct code motion. The only observable change is that propertyName is not computed for declarations whose values contain no time-like substring, which is the intended saving. Confirming this in the PR description or a one-line commit note would close the audit cleanly.

issues.description: Optimization is a local guard, not a decomposition — the rule body still complects scope-check, parse, walk, and report
issues.detail: This patch is a legitimate local speedup: skip the expensive parse on declarations that obviously contain no time token. But the rule body still intermingles 'is this declaration in scope' (property name, ignore list, delay handling) with 'parse the value' with 'walk parsed nodes and report.' A cleaner shape pushes both the 'does this value mention a time' check and the 'is this property in scope' check to the edge before parsing. The PR does the first half of that; the second half is also available and would compose. Not blocking — naming the next move so the optimization doesn't look finished.

issues.description: Property-name lookup could move even earlier for additional rejection
issues.detail: decl.prop.toLowerCase() + vendor.unprefixed() is now only paid when HAS_TIME matches, which is good. But propertyName is still computed for every time-bearing declaration even when the rule will not act on that property at all. The set of properties the rule actually cares about is knowable; a property-name filter would be a second cheap rejection before any parsing. Not required for this PR, just naming the next move.

issues.description: Changeset description is uninformative — states the what but not the why or mechanism
issues.detail: 'Fixed: time-min-milliseconds performance' is accurate but thin. It tells the reader nothing about magnitude, mechanism, or risk. Two more words ('avoid parsing declarations without a time token' or 'early-exit on a regex pre-check') would tell the next maintainer why this diff exists without making them open the PR, and would let a future reader reason about the change without re-deriving it from the diff.

issues.description: Regex is anchorless and broader than CSS <time> grammar; could be tightened to communicate intent
issues.detail: /\dm?s/i with the /i flag is correct (CSS units are case-insensitive), but the predicate also matches 'gs', 'es', '7s' inside identifiers, var() fallbacks, content: literals, url()s, custom properties, or constructed strings — anything the downstream parser must still reject. A more precise form like /\d(?:ms|s)\b/i or one matching the actual time-value grammar would make the invariant obvious by inspection. Harmless for correctness (false positives fall through to the slow path), but the looseness was not justified in the changeset.

issues.description: Same prefilter shape will likely want to be shared if other time-rules adopt it
issues.detail: This is exactly the Unix-filter shape: cheap stateless test on the input string, short-circuit before expensive parsing. If the umbrella issue (#6869) covers other time-related rules, the same prefilter will reappear. Worth noting — not blocking — that a single exported predicate (e.g., hasTimeToken(value)) composed by each rule beats copy-paste regexes drifting apart. Leave inline for now; promote on the second copy.

synthesis.summary: All six reviewers accept the patch as a correct, well-scoped fast-path optimization: a cheap regex pre-filter (/\\dm?s/i) short-circuits the expensive valueParser call on declarations whose values cannot possibly contain a CSS <time> token, and the propertyName/vendor.unprefixed computation is correctly moved past the early-return so the cheap path stays cheap. The single strongest cross-cutting claim — flagged by every reviewer — is that the constant name HAS_TIME overstates the regex's actual postcondition (it's a conservative over-approximation, not an authoritative predicate), and at minimum needs a one-line comment or a rename to MAY_CONTAIN_TIME/MAYBE_HAS_TIME/LIKELY_HAS_TIME. The strongest preserved disagreement is on severity of the missing invariant: Dijkstra calls it P1 ('TESTED-NOT-PROVED — accept only with a comment naming the precondition and/or a tighter regex') and Knuth concurs at P1 ('UNDER-AUDITED'), while Liskov, Hickey, Torvalds, and Pike treat it as a P2 spec-hygiene/naming note and would ship as-is. A secondary split: Knuth wants a benchmark number before calling this a finished performance fix; Torvalds, Hickey, and Pike are satisfied without measurement on the strength of the obvious cost model.
